metricDefinitions.elapsedMs: Wall-clock milliseconds. Fresh mode, every client: from just before the first client process is spawned to the close of the last one, measured by bench/compare/measure.mjs (so it includes process start-up: node and module load for ply, every git child for git). Reused mode, git: the same, over the measured steps only (the set-up clone is not timed). Reused mode, ply: performance.now() around the one measured call inside the already-warm process, so it excludes process start-up; this models a long-lived service, and is not comparable with a fresh-mode figure.
metricDefinitions.peakPssBytes: Peak, over samples, of the sum of Pss from /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup across every process in the client's session (the client is spawned as a session leader; git-remote-http, index-pack, pack-objects, sed and every other descendant inherit the session). PSS divides each shared page among all the processes mapping it, so the sum does not double-count the git binary or fork-shared pages inside the tree; but it also discounts pages shared with processes outside the tree (the node binary shared with the node processes of the harness, the git binary shared with the git processes of the server), so it understates a client that would otherwise run alone. Read it with peakRssSumBytes: the memory a tree needs lies between the two. It is sampled (interval reported per sample as memory.sampleIntervalMs), so it is a lower bound: a peak between two samples, or a process that lives shorter than one interval, is missed. The server (git http-backend and its children) and the harness are not in the session and are not counted. Linux only; null with memory.unavailable set elsewhere. ply reused mode: the peak covers the whole process, warm-up call included.
metricDefinitions.peakRssSumBytes: Peak, over the same samples, of the sum of Rss across the session's processes. Shared pages are counted once per process, so this is an upper bound for a multi-process client (git) and the plain RSS of a one-process client (ply). Sampled, like the PSS sum.
metricDefinitions.maxProcessHwmBytes: The largest VmHWM (the kernel's own per-process peak RSS, from /proc/<pid>/status) seen for any single process of the session. This is the figure `/usr/bin/time -v` or getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN) would report (the largest process, not the sum); a lower bound for the same sampling reason, though tighter, since the kernel keeps the high-water mark between samples.
metricDefinitions.plySelfMaxRssBytes: ply only: process.resourceUsage().maxRSS read by the client process just before it exits (the kernel's exact ru_maxrss). Compared with maxProcessHwmBytes of the same sample it shows the sampler's shortfall.
metricDefinitions.requests: HTTP requests the server received for the repository under test during the measured steps.
metricDefinitions.requestBytes: Request line + request headers (rebuilt from the raw header list) + request body as received after transfer decoding, summed over those requests. A gzip-encoded body is counted compressed, as sent. Excludes chunked framing and TCP/IP.
metricDefinitions.responseBytes: Status line + response headers + response body as written by the server, summed over those requests. Excludes chunked framing and TCP/IP.
metricDefinitions.fetchPackBytes: Pack bytes downloaded: the sum of side-band channel 1 payloads after the `packfile` section header in protocol v2 upload-pack responses. null when no fetch response carried a pack, or a response could not be parsed.
metricDefinitions.pushPackBytes: Pack bytes uploaded: the receive-pack request body after the command list's flush packet (after gunzip when the client gzip-encoded the request). null for a read.

statistics: median, min, max, q1, q3 of the accepted samples; quantiles by linear interpolation between order statistics (R type 7). n is `accepted`.
caveats: Loopback only: client and server share one machine and one kernel, with no latency, loss or bandwidth limit. These timings do not predict WAN latency; over a real network round trips and bytes weigh more and CPU weighs less. Use the request counts and byte totals, which do not depend on the link, to reason about that.

This does not establish Cloudflare Workers memory usage. ply is measured here as a Node process (V8 heap, Node runtime, undici); a Worker isolate has a different baseline and a different accounting. bench/worker-mem measures that on the platform.
Process memory is dominated by runtime baselines at these sizes: see baselines.nodeIdle for what a node process that imports ply and does nothing costs.
The server is git http-backend behind a Node CGI shim on the same machine and competes with the clients for CPU. Hosted services (pack caches, bitmaps, CDNs) behave differently.
Native git also leaves a usable local clone behind; ply leaves nothing. The tasks are equal in their effect on the server and in the bytes read, not in what remains on the client.
Elapsed time includes whatever else the machine was doing; environment.loadavg records the load before and after the run.

ply.label: ply
ply.description: One fresh node process calling ply (readFile streamed to a file; editFile). Reused mode: the same process first performs the same task against the one-commit-behind copy (unmeasured warm-up: module load, JIT, a kept-alive connection, learned server quirks), then the measured call. ply keeps no repository state between calls; its optional pack cache is not exercised.
